svg.aria-label: A contents mockup for the TEGE player's manual: nine chapters and three appendices with their sections, page numbers, audience markers, and a status column showing which parts are written.
svg.title: TEGE manual, chapters and sections
svg.desc: Structure drawn in the pack-in manual idiom: numbered chapters in navy squares, sections on gold squares, dot leaders to page numbers, audience markers in the margin, and a status column using the verdict marks.

g.inkscape:label: 10 Title
g.text: Chapters and sections. Structure mockup in the pack-in manual idiom.

g.inkscape:label: 20 Column one
g.text: Before you start: the one rule
The rail, and its three bands
Plants, and why they go last
Wind, and what it does not push
An empty save list must say so

g.inkscape:label: 30 Column two

g.text: Simulate touch before you send it
Scanning, and how big a group
Nine chapters, three appendices, about 86 pages.
Chapters 1 to 7 run as one walkthrough. 8 and 9 stand alone.

g.inkscape:label: 40 Key and status
g.text: Depth is a coloured square, not a type size
Open the book anywhere and you know your depth without reading a word.
The margin number says who the chapter is for
plays with a switch and a gaze tracker
All three markers are the SAME navy.
Only the numeral changes. Our hues already
mean works, caution and missing. Spending
them on audience would break the system.
Three boxes interrupt the text, and only three

g.inkscape:label: status rows
g.text: written in full, as Player Two's walkthrough
framed against verified anchors, not drafted
not started. Appendix A exists as ENGINE_FACTS
The same three marks that appear inside the manual also describe the manual. That is deliberate:
a reader who learns them on this page can read a status and a warning with the same glance.
Running head names the chapter, so a reader
who opens in the middle is never lost.
Page number in a chip at the foot, publication
name opposite. The two swap on facing pages.

g.inkscape:label: 99 Footer
g.text: Fashioned after the pack-in manuals rather than the one-page designs, because this is the reader-facing artifact: read once in order, then used as a reference forever.
Page numbers are a proposal for pacing, not a measurement. Chapters 2 to 7 already exist as manual/10-first-timer.md.
